definitions.explanation: Third person singular pronoun for males.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
{彼|かれ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{聞|き}いてみよう→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
{彼|かれ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦{早|はや}く→速い／早い：00514_hayai⟧⟦{起|お}きて→起きる：00521_okiru⟧⟦{走|はし}っている→走る：00519_hashiru⟧。
examples.english: He gets up early every morning and goes running.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{話|はな}せる→話す：00467_hanasu⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧、⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{頼|たよ}りにされている→頼る：02069_tayoru⟧。
examples.english: He can speak both Japanese and English, so he is relied on a lot at the company.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{優|やさ}しい→優しい：02640_yasashii⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{困|こま}っている→困る：00861_komaru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{助|たす}けて→助ける：00895_tasukeru⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: He is a kind person, and whenever someone is in trouble, he always helps them.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧{彼|かれ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。

examples.english: I went to see a movie with my boyfriend.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{誕生日|たんじょうび}→誕生日：02910_tanjoubi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{何|なに}→何：00498_nani⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげたら→あげる：00546_ageru⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{迷|まよ}っている→迷う：02426_mayou⟧。
examples.english: I'm wondering what to give my boyfriend for his birthday.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三年|さんねん}→三年：10984_sannen⟧⟦{付|つ}き{合|あ}っている→付き合う：02291_tsukiau⟧⟦けど→けど：09477_kedo⟧、⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{紹介|しょうかい}していない→紹介：01432_shoukai⟧。
examples.english: I've been dating my boyfriend for three years, but I still haven't introduced him to my family.

notes:
{彼|かれ} has two distinct uses: as a third-person pronoun meaning 'he/him' and as a noun meaning 'boyfriend.'

AS PRONOUN:
Less frequently used than 'he' in English. Japanese typically omits pronouns when the referent is clear from context, and using the person's name is often preferred over {彼|かれ}. Overusing {彼|かれ} can sound unnatural.

AS 'BOYFRIEND':
- {彼|かれ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧: to have a boyfriend
- {彼|かれ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧: to get a boyfriend
- ⟦{彼氏|かれし}→彼氏：06456_kareshi⟧: boyfriend (casual, very common alternative)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧: she / girlfriend (female counterpart)
- ⟦{彼|かれ}ら→彼ら：01802_karera⟧: they (plural, for groups including males)
